thread:
marta: FYI started the burn/soak on new-eu6 cluster (gpu-pool-v2). seeing autoscaler drop pods mid-ramp, leads to increased latency spikes. tagging eng-sre for visibility.

ryan: coming in — what autoscaler are we using? k8s HPA or cluster-autoscaler?

marta: cluster-autoscaler with CA-managed nodepools. HPA on the inference service scales replicas to GPU utilization.

sam: can you paste the CA logs? and the HPA config? maybe scale-down is too aggressive.

marta: paste ->
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference rt-infer -o yaml
# targetCPU: 40
# targetMemory: 60Mi
# minReplicas: 2
# maxReplicas: 40
``` 
CA flags: --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m (defaults)

ryan: k8s defaults are often aggressive for GPU workloads because node startup + model warmup >> cpu probe. increase scale-down delay and unneeded-time to 20m maybe 30m.

karen: also check our readiness probe and preStop hooks. if pods become 'NotReady' during model init, CA may think nodes are underutilized and kill them.

marta: good call. current readiness is http /health (returns ready only after model loaded). model load ~2.5m for 80B quantized.

alex: two quick mitigations: 1) bump CA --scale-down-unneeded-time to 30m and --scale-down-delay-after-add to 30m, 2) add annotation to critical nodepools to prevent CA from aggressively evicting: cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true" during soak.

sam: for step testing: we did a ramp test 0% -> 25% -> 50% traffic. where exactly are pods dropping? during step 50%?

marta: timeline: at 50% increase we see spike in pending pods for ~90s, then CA adds nodes, pods schedule, but 30-60s after they become Ready we see ~2 pods evicted from older nodes and then another wave of scheduling that creates a short window with fewer replicas -> qps surge on remaining pods and latency spike.

ryan: that sounds like churn from bin-packing + descheduling. check Kube scheduler logs and pod disruption budgets. any PDBs on the inference deployments?

marta: PDB allows 1 unavailable on a 10 replica service.

sam: reduce PDB temporarily to 0 unavailable so we don't evict? careful. alternative: increase minReplicas for HPA during soak (pin at 6) to avoid dips.

karen: also check node autoscaling cooldown with cloud provider. sometimes cloud provider reclaims or merges preemptible capacity and CA sees capacity gap and overshoots then scales down rapidly. What instance types are we using in gpu-pool-v2?

marta: using g4dn-equivalent preemptible for burst, and rtx-a5000 reserved for baseline. Preemptible termination notices are frequent in the window.

alex: preemptibles complicate. Recommendation: during region bring-up keep baseline on reserved instances for first 24h soak, use preemptible only for >70% load, and keep buffer of +2 reserved nodes. Cost hit but reduces churn.

marta: noted. cost question: if we keep reserved for 24h extra, runbook cost delta ~ +$1.4k (eu region) for the soak window. is that acceptable?

sam: yes for initial bring-up. we can amortize and credit back from launch budget.

ci-bot: [deploy] rollout of manifest gpu-pool-v2 config #1772 succeeded in 3m 12s.

ryan: other observable: KV cache cold misses cause long model init token generation—makes the new pods slow to reach steady-state throughput. we should prime cache on new nodes.

marta: how do we prime? run a background warmup job that hits the model with typical prefix sets (from /infra/priming/prompt-sets).

sam: exact command we used earlier:
```bash
python infra/tools/warmup.py --pool gpu-pool-v2 --queries ./priming/standard_prompts.json --concurrency 10 --duration 10m
``` 
This nails common KV prefixes and reduces first-50-token latency by ~60%.

karen: add that warmup to the runbook step 3 (after nodes ready, before traffic shift).

marta: agree. draft runbook checklist so we can hand off to oncall: 1) provision nodepool (reserved baseline + preemptible burst), 2) verify networking & egress rules, 3) smoke deploy inference image (canary 1 pod), 4) run warmup job, 5) run gradual soak: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% (10-15m hold each), 6) monitor P95 latency, GPU utilization, pod count, CA events, 7) if churn >3 events in 15m rollback to previous nodepool config, 8) keep reserved baseline for 24h, 9) cost owner notification.

ryan: add step: validate autoscaler flags and HPA minReplicas pinned during the ramp. Also verify that scale-down-delay and scale-down-unneeded-time both >= 20m.

marta: adding. also adding single PromQL queries for quick dashboard:
- pod churn: increase(rate(kube_pod_deletion_total[5m]))
- gpu_util: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization[5m])
- scale events: increase(cluster_autoscaler_events_total[10m])
- latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

sam: can we expose a temporary Autoscaler dashboard link in the runbook? point to https://grafana.company.internal/d/auto/ca?orgId=1&var-cluster=eu6

marta: done. adding links + threshold badges. thresholds: P95 latency < 350ms, GPU util 50-80% during soak, scale events <2 per 10m.

oncall-bot: @channel scheduled handoff to oncall @ryan at 18:00 UTC.

ryan: I'll take handoff. final asks before I assume: confirm warmup job artifact, confirm CA flags pushed, confirm reserved baseline set to +2.

marta: warmup artifact pushed: s3://infra-artifacts/eu6/warmup-v1.tar.gz, CA flags updated in cluster-config/gpu-pool-v2.yaml, reserved baseline +2.

karen: also log the cost owner: finance-alert@redwood.com and set a budget flag on the task in linear.

sam: last note: after 24h soak run an automated analysis job: compare token-level cost and P95 vs stage region. if regression >10% open an incident.

marta: putting post-soak eval in the runbook (evals/eu6/soak-24h-report).

ryan: sounds good. I will run the traffic shifts manually and watch the dashboard. ping here if anything odd. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks all, will post updates. :rocket:
